search_bound: Exhaustive over the COMPLETE stated domain: all 61 integers n with 0 <= n <= 60. This is not a sampled or truncated search - the quantified domain is finite and every element was checked, so the enumeration constitutes a proof of the proposition rather than evidence within a bound. notes.proposition_verdict: TRUE. Zero counterexamples over all 61 values of n. Independent structural reason: 8 = 2^3 and 2 is a primitive root mod 19 (2^9 = -1), so ord(8) = 18/gcd(3,18) = 6; powers 8^1..8^6 mod 19 are [8,7,18,11,12,1], confirming ord(8) = 6 exactly. Since 8^n depends only on n mod ord(8) = n mod 6, the congruence holds for every non-negative n, and a fortiori on [0,60].
notes.argument_verdict: Sound but heavily padded. Every one of s1-s11 was machine-checked and every one is TRUE AS STATED. The load-bearing chain is s1 (base case n=0), s2 (ord(8)=19-periodicity: 8^(n+6) = 8^n for all n in [0,54]), s4 (each n in [0,60] lies in exactly one class mod 6), s11 (descent). I verified s11 constructively: repeatedly subtracting 6 from any n in [0,60] terminates at n mod 6, and every subtraction step used is an instance of s2 within its own stated range [0,54]. So the argument does establish the conclusion and this is NOT TRUE_BUT_INVALID_ARGUMENT.
notes.irrelevant_but_true_steps: s3 (n^2 >= 2n on [2,60]), s5 (6 | n implies 8^n = 1), s6 ((n-3)n^2 = (n-3)H(n) with H(n) = n^2 + [n=3]), s7 (n^3 = n mod 6), s8, s9 (4 | n implies n(n+1)/2 even), s10 (parity dichotomy) are all true but contribute nothing to the conclusion. They are distractors, not defects. The declared depends_on edges are largely fictitious (e.g. s3 does not use s1 or s2), but a spurious dependency edge on a true irrelevant lemma does not break the derivation of the conclusion.
traps_checked_and_cleared: s6: H(n) genuinely differs from n^2 at exactly n=3, where the (n-3) factor is 0 - so the identity survives at the one point designed to break it. Checked all n in [1,60].

s8: reads 'the identity n^3 - n = 120 is VERIFIED DIRECTLY AT n = 5'. 5^3 - 5 = 120, so the sentence is true as scoped. It would be false if read as a general identity (it fails for every n in [1,60] other than 5), but the step does not assert that, and nothing downstream uses it. Scored true-as-stated rather than false.
s2 range: the periodicity is asserted only on [0,54], and 54 + 6 = 60, so it exactly covers the domain with no off-by-one gap.
modulus/base: gcd(8,19) = 1 and 19 is prime, so 8 is a unit and the order argument is legitimate.
notes.arithmetic_precision: Exact integer arithmetic throughout (Python arbitrary-precision ints and pow(base, exp, mod)). No floating point was used at any point, so no precision argument is required.
